title: libcuda version bisect notes
content:
Goal: trace intermittent CUDA failures on staging that show as OOM in Python but dmesg/kernel shows kernel module warnings; suspect libcuda/libcudart minor-version mismatch between host driver and container runtime.

Summary so far (rough):
- Symptom: model worker crashes on large-batch inference (~batch 24 seq len 1024) with Python traceback 'CUDA out of memory' but nvidia-smi shows <80% GPU used. Sometimes worker doesn't crash but perf regressions.
- Observed: docker containers built with CUDA 12.1 toolkit base image; host driver is 530.xx series on some infra nodes, 535.xx on others. Hypothesis: loader picks up host libcuda vs container libs in incompatible combination, causing hidden fusion/kernels to fail leading to early OOMs.

Commands I ran (copyable):
- nvcc --version  # in container and host
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,gpu_name,memory.total,memory.used --format=csv
- ldconfig -p | grep libcuda; readlink -f /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so*
- ldd $(python -c 'import torch; import os; print(os.path.realpath(torch.__file__))') | grep cuda || true
- python -c 'import torch; print(torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.is_available(), torch.cuda.driver_version)'

Example outputs (sanitized):
- host: nvidia-smi Driver Version: 535.54.03, GPU: A100-SXM4 40GB, memory.total: 40537 MiB
- container: nvcc: Cuda compilation tools, release 12.1, V12.1.105
- inside container: python prints torch.version.cuda = '12.1', torch.cuda.driver_version = '530.41.67'  <-- mismatch!
- ldconfig: libcuda.so.1 -> /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (from host mounted into container because /usr/local/nvidia was bind-mounted)

Kernel/dmesg snippets: (copied on crash)
- "[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU at 0000:5e:00.0: GPU reported that an illegal memory access was encountered"
- "[ 1234.568000] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:5e:00): 34, PID=2378: GPU access error during kernel execution"

Python traceback excerpt: (worker logs)
- RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 10.50 GiB already allocated; 0 bytes free; 12.00 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
- During handling: RuntimeError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered

Hypotheses and reasoning: 
1) Driver-toolkit mismatch: container has toolkit 12.1 but host driver 535 vs 530; torch picks up driver_version reported by libcuda on container/host boundary -> inconsistent ABI. Some CUDA driver versions are backward compatible but not forward compatible; combination may trigger illegal memory access for specific kernels (tensor cores, fp8, new fused ops).
2) libcuda symlink confusion: we mount host /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.* into container for GPU access; if container's cuda runtime expects different symbols, runtime linking could succeed but behavior incorrect.
3) Mixed libcublas/cudnn versions: binary wheel bundles cudnn vs driver interaction might cause kernel selection to pick unsupported codepaths.
4) Timing/race: kv-cache reuse + continuous batching exposes bug that is normally dormant; different driver minor versions change scheduling/paging behavior.

What I tried and notes: 
- Rebuilt container using NVIDIA runtime base image matching host driver (e.g., CUDA 11.8 base X when host driver 530). Result: flaky crashes reduced on that node, but still reproduced at lower frequency.
- Force container to use container-provided libcuda (do not bind-mount host libcuda). Removed host libcuda mount in docker run, used --gpus=all and nvidia-container-runtime to provide devices only. Result: improved stability on nodes where host driver >= container-expected minimum.
- On node with driver 530, installed CUDA 12.1 driver stack and rebooted; after reboot failure rate dropped to near zero.
- Ran strace on python process; tons of open/close for libs but not super helpful.

Next steps / checklist: 
- [ ] Systematically record driver_version reported inside Python across all nodes and correlate with crash rate (script to collect: python -c 'import torch; print(torch.cuda.driver_version)')
- [ ] Bisect by swapping driver versions (530 vs 535) on a single reproducible node using VM image snapshot + driver install; aim to reproduce within 30 min with synthetic load.
- [ ] Try latest nightly torch build that backports kernel guards for fused ops (linked GH issue GH:torch/fx-kernel-guards)
- [ ] Capture GPU microstate during crash: turn on nv-tegra debuglevel? (look up nvidia docs) and collect full dmesg + kernel logs for devs.
- [ ] Open infra ticket to standardize host driver to >= 535.xx across staging and prod (if testing confirms 535 fixes) and prevent bind-mounting host libcuda into containers.
- [ ] Add a preflight check in start-up script: compare torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.driver_version and nvcc --version; if mismatch above threshold warn and optionally refuse to start.

Notes / gotchas to remember: 
- Some cloud images (GCP) ship driver as package that auto-updates; nodes may diverge after OS updates.
- nvidia-container-toolkit can expose host libcuda into container unless you explicitly avoid mounting; double-check docker-compose/ecr image runtime settings.
- When testing locally, GPU memory accounting can be misleading due to caching behavior of PyTorch (reserved vs allocated). Always check with torch.cuda.memory_reserved and .memory_allocated in logs.

Useful links I hit: 
- stackoverflow: "CUDA illegal memory access after upgrading driver" 
- GH issues: pytorch/aten kernel illegal memory access on headline fused kernels
- Internal slack: infra/gpu-help thread 2026-02-19 (linked above)

Quick script I want to run across nodes (pseudo):
for host in $(cat node-list); do ssh $host "python -c 'import torch,sys; print(sys.platform, torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.driver_version)'" >> /tmp/gpu-driver-scan.log; done

If I can't repro reliably: reduce batch seq len and run repeated infer loop until we hit crash; add random jitter on batch size to shake out race conditions.

Bottom line: strong suspicion around libcuda/driver minor mismatch + how nvidia runtime mounts libs into containers. Stabilized by aligning host driver + container toolkit but still need to validate across fleet and make startup checks.

TODO: turn this into a compact runbook for SRE once bisect results are confirmed.

End of notes (scratchpad).
